subject: humanities
passage: Completed in 1885, the Home Insurance Building in Chicago rose ten stories, a great height for its time. Before then, the outer walls of a tall building had to carry its full weight, so the lower walls needed to be extremely thick. The Home Insurance Building was different: a frame made of iron and steel held up the structure. Its walls could therefore be thinner, and many historians consider it the first skyscraper.
stem: According to the text, how was the Home Insurance Building different from earlier tall buildings?

choices.A: Its outer walls were made thicker so that they could support more floors.
choices.B: It was the first building in Chicago to rise more than ten stories.
choices.C: It had more windows than any other office building of its time.
choices.D: Its weight was carried by a metal frame rather than by its walls.

explanation.why: The text says that in earlier tall buildings "the outer walls . . . had to carry its full weight," but in the Home Insurance Building "a frame made of iron and steel held up the structure." The difference is that a metal frame, not the walls, carried the load.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says the opposite: because of the frame, its walls could be thinner.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says the building had ten stories, not more than ten, and never ranks it among Chicago buildings.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text never mentions windows.
explanation.D: Correct. The text contrasts weight-bearing walls in earlier buildings with the iron and steel frame that held up this one.
